question: In a purely capacitive AC circuit, the power consumed over a complete cycle is _______.
solution:
The correct answer is __zero__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In a purely capacitive AC circuit__, the current leads the voltage by 90 degrees.
 
• The power consumed over a complete cycle is zero because the energy stored in the capacitor during one-half of the cycle is returned to the source during the other half.
 
• Thus, no net energy is consumed over a complete cycle in a purely capacitive AC circuit.
 
• Power in such circuits is reactive power, not real power.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Resistive Circuit:**
 
 
• In a purely resistive AC circuit, the voltage and current are in phase.
 
• The power consumed is real power and is not zero.
 
 
 
• **Inductive Circuit:**
 
 
• The current lags the voltage by 90 degrees in a purely inductive AC circuit.
 
• The power consumed over a complete cycle is also zero as energy is returned to the source.
